## picomatch.diff.trailing-slash
# A trailing `/` (10 rows)
# A trailing `/` ends in an empty name: `a/*` matches `a/`, `a` does not match
# `a/` (GLOB_SPEC §9.5, §14.2). The library ignores a trailing `/`, or needs
# one on both sides.
# picomatch: no-match  [test/globstars.js:388]
a/**/*	a/	match	dot=false
# picomatch: no-match  [test/globstars.js:389]
a/**/**/*	a/	match	dot=false
# picomatch: no-match  [test/globstars.js:390]

*/*	a/	match	dot=false

## picomatch.diff.we-reject-UnterminatedClass
# A `[` that never closes (7 rows)
# globstar reads classes by POSIX's rules (GLOB_SPEC §8.5): a `]` first in the
# list is literal, and a class cannot hold `/`, so a `[` with no closing `]`
# after that is a parse error. The library accepts the pattern, as literal
# text or with the class crossing `/`; its answer is the row's comment.
# picomatch: match  [test/api.picomatch.js:266]
foo[/]bar	foo/bar	err:UnterminatedClass	dot=false
# picomatch: no-match  [test/bash.js:723]
[]	a	err:UnterminatedClass	dot=false
# picomatch: no-match  [test/bash.js:724]
[abc	[	err:UnterminatedClass	dot=false
# picomatch: match  [test/brackets.js:18]
foo[/]bar[/]	foo/bar/	err:UnterminatedClass	dot=false
# picomatch: match  [test/brackets.js:19]
foo[/]bar[/]baz	foo/bar/baz	err:UnterminatedClass	dot=false
# picomatch: match  [test/regex-features.js:110]
a[c	a[c	err:UnterminatedClass	dot=false
# picomatch: match  [test/regex-features.js:111]
a[	a[	err:UnterminatedClass	dot=false

## picomatch.diff.backslash
# A backslash in the pattern (3 rows)
# `\X` is the literal `X` for every `X` (GLOB_SPEC §4.1), inside classes too,
# and a path is never unescaped. The library gives some escapes another
# meaning (`\b`, `\w`), keeps the backslash, or unescapes the path.
# picomatch: match  [test/bash.js:88]
\*	\*	no-match	dot=false
# picomatch: no-match  [test/bash.js:544]
a[\b]c	abc	match	dot=false
# picomatch: match  [test/regex-features.js:10]
a\b	a	no-match	dot=false

## picomatch.diff.class-or-literal
# A class matching its own text (3 rows)
# picomatch and micromatch let a bracket expression match either one of its
# characters or its own literal text, so `*[1]` matches `copy [1]`. A class
# matches one character (GLOB_SPEC §8).
# picomatch: match  [test/special-characters.js:347]
**/*[1]	foo/bar - copy [1]	no-match	dot=false
# picomatch: match  [test/special-characters.js:348]
**/*[1]	foo/bar - foo + bar - copy [1]	no-match	dot=false
# picomatch: match  [test/special-characters.js:353]
a [b] c	a [b] c	no-match	dot=false
